notes.title: Developer Blog #53 - Burn Baby, Burn!
notes.content:
[url=https://i.gyazo.com/5b4de93143339240e22341411fca8328.gif]Pak40 Firing Animation[/url]

The flamethrower has been considered, throughout warfare, as a cruel and merciless weapon. It was widely used during the Second World War, and it’s terrifying damage potential accurately represents the horror and fear the soldiers lived in the battlefields. On our 53rd blog we’d like to talk about this a little further.

[h1]A nasty sting[/h1]

Flamethrowers are one of the deadliest weapons at close range. Upon getting in contact with a burst, a soldier is guaranteed to get burnt to death, regardless of his skill or protective bulletproof gear. Not only soldiers, but vehicles, fortifications, and ultimately the whole landscape can be turned into decaying ash and smoke.

But flamethrowers aren’t safe either! Fire does not know of friend or foe, you run the risk of burning your own equipment. You should also consider how the fire can spread to ensure you won’t be burning your own areas.  

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/b9ce80910a36cf60f937302c8a53a82864fa34de.jpg[/img]
[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/b9ce80910a36cf60f937302c8a53a82864fa34de.jpg]HD Link[/url]

[h1]Increased burning times[/h1]

We increased how long objects last until they are finally consumed by fire. This brings extra immersion into the battlefield, and makes a flamethrower presence pretty obvious!

[h1]Performance[/h1]

Fire effects, especially in large numbers, are an obvious concern with regards to performance. So we spent a lot of work minimising the particle densities to be able to deliver maximum playability without a decrease in performance.

[h1]Remodelled mechanic[/h1]

We turned flamethrowers into semi-automatic burst weapons. So every time you click on a target, a burst is thrown at the enemy. If you want a constant burst, keep clicking at your preferred rate. This brings us two key advantages. For one, it more accurately represents how the flamethrowers were used in war. Often, such a dense cloud of black smoke did not allow you to see if your burst was going in the right direction, or you just wanted to deliver the right amount of burning fluid. So the obvious solution was to shoot in bursts.

https://youtu.be/pzioV10sSAU

Secondly, a burst mechanic allows you to more accurately quantify how much fuel you are using knowing how many shots you’re making. Flamethrowers such as the Flammenwerfer model 1939 only had 12 liters of fuel. In this way you can play more conservatively.

Finally, we are also aware some players like to  grab their flamethrowers and start charging the enemy while rotating about and launching a constant fireball stream in all directions. So now we offer you the charming opportunity to be a bit more civilised and reconsider such suicide runs with our burst-mechanic.

[h1]Flame vehicles[/h1]

You can also choose to deliver hell on earth by tracked vehicles! They are obviously more protected than an infantryman, but equally they are more expensive. We are currently implementing the OT-34 obr-43 and the Hetzer/Flamm. Please let us know, if you want some more, and we will consider them.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/c93b8014a2d9a9b40c4adb83ac8c776b3df779c2.jpg[/img]
[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/c93b8014a2d9a9b40c4adb83ac8c776b3df779c2.jpg]HD Link[/url]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/e6885d6e895132ea5eed69aa8cc270567f17b2a4.jpg[/img]
[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/e6885d6e895132ea5eed69aa8cc270567f17b2a4.jpg]HD Link[/url]

notes.title: Developer Blog #47 - Armour 2.0
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/1acc59d93c25e597fa4642be3431ae90d750e1e0.png[/img]

Greetings! This week we will continue discussing the subject you voted for the most: Ballistic and Ammunition system overhaul. In the last developer blog (#46) we explained the various shells that cannons and tank guns will use. Today we will discuss armour types and their ability to resist penetration.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/3a322438c1b69916fa99d11fdae7ebe1decfecfa.jpg[/img]

[h1]Introduction[/h1]

It is important to note that the same ballistics calculations are used for both small arms and large projectiles. This includes information such as: Shell Type, Caliber, Speed, Trajectory, Penetration, and Damage. Likewise, the armour calculations include Armour Slope (or angle) and Thickness. In the future, Armour Type (RHA, FHA, Cast, High Hardness) and Armour Quality (flaws) may be included as well. (Depending on the results of internal testing.)

Now, the game may use the familiar UI colors to indicate if a shell will successfully penetrate armour (Green = Yes, Yellow = Maybe and Red = No), but we have implemented major changes to the calculations and formulas happening behind the scenes. To help demonstrate results of these changes, our game mechanic engineer has created a web based armour resistance calculator specifically for GoH. We will cover this in more detail at the end of this dev blog.

[h1]The Slope Effect[/h1]

All armour plates have a specific amount of physical thickness, often measured in millimeters. For example, the front plate of a Soviet T-34 medium tank is 45mm thick. The armour plate is also sloped at angle of 60° from the vertical. Because of the tilted armor, the relative thickness increases and projectiles must go through more steel to penetrate. In the case of the T-34, relative thickness is 90mm. 45mm / Cosine (60°) = 90mm. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/aa366946345b74c56c5bccbb59bc8d63acacd954.png[/img]
While the equation is mathematically correct, it does not account for the effect that sloped armour has on various shell types. This effect often increases resistance above the relative armour thickness.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/2197783fcbf1eaf062fa45c6a24e72cfa5917c1e.png[/img]
The "slope effect" is defined as: the multiplier that converts an angled impact penetration to an equivalent resistance at 0°. To paraphrase, the slope effect is a number (usually greater than 1) that is multiplied by the physical thickness, to give the real penetration resistance as if the armour plate had no slope. Thickness x Slope Effect = Armour Resistance @ 0°. Since all of the penetration data we use for guns is at 0°, we also want armour effectiveness data at 0°. This may be difficult to understand so we will use the T-34 example again.

Lets use an example of the  T-34 front plate versus a German 75mm APCBC shell. After running slope effect formula  we get a value of 2.7. If we multiply this by the armour plate thickness we get a equivalent resistance of ~122mm at 0°.  45mm x 2.7 = ~122mm. Meaning, the T-34 front plate that is 45mm thick and with a 60° slope resists penetration from the 75mm APCBC shell like a 122mm thick armour plate would with a 0° slope.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/aa4cffa763b334a3240c9c6b205e4c8a2f7b109a.png[/img]

This is assuming that the T-34 plate is rolled homogeneous armour (RHA), is perfect quality (no flaws) and has the Brinell Hardness Number (BHN) of 240. We will discuss these armour types and factors next.

*BHN 240 is the hardness of the U.S. Test plate used in ballistic testing in the 1940's. Penetration data has also been converted to how it would perform against standard (RHA) US Test plate, allowing direct comparisons between nations. (Each nation had its own methods for calculating penetration data and it is important that they be converted to a common standard.)


[h1]Armour Types[/h1]

There were several types of armour that World War II Vehicles could be made from. Each nation had its own methods of manufacturing that affected how well the armour resisted penetration.


[h1]Rolled Homogeneous Armour (RHA)[/h1]

(RHA) is cast steel that is hot rolled to a desired thickness. The rolling creates structural changes that help disperse stress loads throughout the plate. It was produced by all nations and is the most common armour type. In game, this is the default armour type and all penetration equations are set with RHA in mind.

 
[h1]Cast Armour[/h1]

Cast Armour is the most basic form of steel armour. Firing test results from several nations indicate that cast armour is less resistant than rolled armor due to beneficial structural changes that take place when armour is rolled.


[h1]Face Hardened Armour (FHA)[/h1]

FHA has a thin outer layer of 450-650 BHN hardness on top of a standard rolled plate. FHA will be the most difficult to implement in game since there is no equation to easily account for its effects against various shell types. (It seems to vary greatly from each shell size and type.) For this reason it is not included in the armour calculator.


[h1]High Hardness Rolled Homogeneous Armour[/h1]

It is best to consider High Hardness armour as a "Type" of armour for our purposes. Armour with a hardness below 375 BHN is expected to have reasonable impact resistance, allowing it to withstand multiple hits without cracking or spalling. As hardness increases above 375 BHN, it becomes brittle and loses penetration resistance when the diameter of projectile (caliber) is equal or greater than the physical thickness of the armour plate. High Hardness is a common feature for Soviet vehicles except for the KV-1 and KV-2.

If we apply the High Hardness multiplier to the previous T-34 example, it would reduces the armour effectives from ~122mm to ~94mm against the German 75mm APCBC shell. (Assuming a BHN value of 450.) This matches German field reports describing the ranges at which T-34s could be defeated by 75mm guns.


[h1]Armour Flaws[/h1]

As the war progressed, important materials for armour production were rationed which would affect armour quality and penetration resistance. Also unskilled labor and poor quality control contributed to armour quality in certain situations. An example would be, American quality control permitted flawed armor in many tanks prior to October 1943, including Sherman front plates. It is possible the British underwent major quality control improvements around the same time. notes.title: Developer Blog #47 - Armour 2.0
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/1acc59d93c25e597fa4642be3431ae90d750e1e0.png[/img]

Greetings! This week we will continue discussing the subject you voted for the most: Ballistic and Ammunition system overhaul. In the last developer blog (#46) we explained the various shells that cannons and tank guns will use. Today we will discuss armour types and their ability to resist penetration.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/3a322438c1b69916fa99d11fdae7ebe1decfecfa.jpg[/img]

[h1]Introduction[/h1]

It is important to note that the same ballistics calculations are used for both small arms and large projectiles. This includes information such as: Shell Type, Caliber, Speed, Trajectory, Penetration, and Damage. Likewise, the armour calculations include Armour Slope (or angle) and Thickness. In the future, Armour Type (RHA, FHA, Cast, High Hardness) and Armour Quality (flaws) may be included as well. (Depending on the results of internal testing.)

Now, the game may use the familiar UI colors to indicate if a shell will successfully penetrate armour (Green = Yes, Yellow = Maybe and Red = No), but we have implemented major changes to the calculations and formulas happening behind the scenes. To help demonstrate results of these changes, our game mechanic engineer has created a web based armour resistance calculator specifically for GoH. We will cover this in more detail at the end of this dev blog.

[h1]The Slope Effect[/h1]

All armour plates have a specific amount of physical thickness, often measured in millimeters. For example, the front plate of a Soviet T-34 medium tank is 45mm thick. The armour plate is also sloped at angle of 60° from the vertical. Because of the tilted armor, the relative thickness increases and projectiles must go through more steel to penetrate. In the case of the T-34, relative thickness is 90mm. 45mm / Cosine (60°) = 90mm. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/aa366946345b74c56c5bccbb59bc8d63acacd954.png[/img]
While the equation is mathematically correct, it does not account for the effect that sloped armour has on various shell types. This effect often increases resistance above the relative armour thickness.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/2197783fcbf1eaf062fa45c6a24e72cfa5917c1e.png[/img]
The "slope effect" is defined as: the multiplier that converts an angled impact penetration to an equivalent resistance at 0°. To paraphrase, the slope effect is a number (usually greater than 1) that is multiplied by the physical thickness, to give the real penetration resistance as if the armour plate had no slope. Thickness x Slope Effect = Armour Resistance @ 0°. Since all of the penetration data we use for guns is at 0°, we also want armour effectiveness data at 0°. This may be difficult to understand so we will use the T-34 example again.

Lets use an example of the  T-34 front plate versus a German 75mm APCBC shell. After running slope effect formula  we get a value of 2.7. If we multiply this by the armour plate thickness we get a equivalent resistance of ~122mm at 0°.  45mm x 2.7 = ~122mm. Meaning, the T-34 front plate that is 45mm thick and with a 60° slope resists penetration from the 75mm APCBC shell like a 122mm thick armour plate would with a 0° slope.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/aa4cffa763b334a3240c9c6b205e4c8a2f7b109a.png[/img]

This is assuming that the T-34 plate is rolled homogeneous armour (RHA), is perfect quality (no flaws) and has the Brinell Hardness Number (BHN) of 240. We will discuss these armour types and factors next.

*BHN 240 is the hardness of the U.S. Test plate used in ballistic testing in the 1940's. Penetration data has also been converted to how it would perform against standard (RHA) US Test plate, allowing direct comparisons between nations. (Each nation had its own methods for calculating penetration data and it is important that they be converted to a common standard.)


[h1]Armour Types[/h1]

There were several types of armour that World War II Vehicles could be made from. Each nation had its own methods of manufacturing that affected how well the armour resisted penetration.


[h1]Rolled Homogeneous Armour (RHA)[/h1]

(RHA) is cast steel that is hot rolled to a desired thickness. The rolling creates structural changes that help disperse stress loads throughout the plate. It was produced by all nations and is the most common armour type. In game, this is the default armour type and all penetration equations are set with RHA in mind.

 
[h1]Cast Armour[/h1]

Cast Armour is the most basic form of steel armour. Firing test results from several nations indicate that cast armour is less resistant than rolled armor due to beneficial structural changes that take place when armour is rolled.


[h1]Face Hardened Armour (FHA)[/h1]

FHA has a thin outer layer of 450-650 BHN hardness on top of a standard rolled plate. FHA will be the most difficult to implement in game since there is no equation to easily account for its effects against various shell types. (It seems to vary greatly from each shell size and type.) For this reason it is not included in the armour calculator.


[h1]High Hardness Rolled Homogeneous Armour[/h1]

It is best to consider High Hardness armour as a "Type" of armour for our purposes. Armour with a hardness below 375 BHN is expected to have reasonable impact resistance, allowing it to withstand multiple hits without cracking or spalling. As hardness increases above 375 BHN, it becomes brittle and loses penetration resistance when the diameter of projectile (caliber) is equal or greater than the physical thickness of the armour plate. High Hardness is a common feature for Soviet vehicles except for the KV-1 and KV-2.

If we apply the High Hardness multiplier to the previous T-34 example, it would reduces the armour effectives from ~122mm to ~94mm against the German 75mm APCBC shell. (Assuming a BHN value of 450.) This matches German field reports describing the ranges at which T-34s could be defeated by 75mm guns.


[h1]Armour Flaws[/h1]

As the war progressed, important materials for armour production were rationed which would affect armour quality and penetration resistance. Also unskilled labor and poor quality control contributed to armour quality in certain situations. An example would be, American quality control permitted flawed armor in many tanks prior to October 1943, including Sherman front plates. It is possible the British underwent major quality control improvements around the same time. Many German Panther and Tiger II tanks suffered from medium to large flaws in their armour (especially Panther Glacis) which contributed to lower than expected penetration resistance.

Again, testing still needs to be done to determine which or if any of the armor types and factors will be in the finished game.

As mentioned before, our game mechanic engineer has created a web based calculator with all the formulas for these armour mechanics built in. You will notice that the default values are from the T-34 example. Feel free to change the various inputs to see the armour resistance change against the various shell types.

[h1]Link [url=https://jscalc.io/calc/2u6dtwLwzxNmqWld]Gates of Hell: Armor Effectiveness Calculator [/url][/h1]

[url=https://jscalc.io/calc/2u6dtwLwzxNmqWld][img]https://s11.postimg.org/tyzvzhogj/Armour_calculator.png[/img][/url]

While there are many sources available on the topic, none are quite as comprehensive as "World War II Ballistics: Armor and Gunnery" by Lorring Rexford Bird and Robert D. Livingston. The full equations for slope, armour and flaw multipliers can be found here, and the converted penetration data. Any formation that cannot be found in the WWII Ballistics book, have been collected from various websites including but not limited to: panzerworld.com , battlefield.ru , wwiivehicles.com , gva.freeweb.hu ... etc.


[h1]Last Note[/h1]

We believe that the redesign of ballistics and armour will make our game unique in the RTS market. We also aim to make the whole system second nature for our players. While we pursue historic authenticity, we do not want it to sacrifice fun and competitive gameplay. No one shall be left behind!

notes.title: Developer Blog #46 - Armour and Shells Part I
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/3898fe570cbbf5612580184749bf4bae8e74e9e4.png[/img]

Hello friends and players! Welcome back. Today we have some juicy news. The polling results are in, and you voted to learn more about the ballistics and ammunitions system overhaul, as well as our realistic armour penetration redesign. There is [b]too much[/b] information in each one of these topics to cover them all in just one developer blog so we will begin Part 1 by discussing gun ammunition.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/a7afd24e2529cdebceff8418a9b0e6a7d92f4ff1.jpg[/img]

[h1]Introduction[/h1]

To understand better how we plan to move forward, it is important to recognize where we are coming from. In previous gem2 games, gun ammunition was largely limited to 2 or 3 shell types: Armor Piercing, High Explosive, and some included higher penetration shells (APCR).

Our goal has been to redesign this system to portray most historically accurate representation of gun ammunition that has ever been in Gem2. This will be achieved through but not limited to the following features.
 
 - Vehicles will come with realistic loadouts for their time period, both in composition and overall quantity.
 - Each shell type will have its own muzzle velocity and other properties, meaning that a gun has a different behaviour for each shell type depending on historical data.
 - Newly added slope effects, Thickness / Diameter Ratios, and Normalization functions for EACH shell type and caliber size. (This will be explained later in further detail)
 

[h1]Shells Types[/h1]

Vehicles will rarely have more than 3-4 types of shells in their inventory, so they will all be useful and have their role. Although there are many types of ammunition that were designed throughout WW2, in GoH we have a structure of different classes that is colour-coded for ease of use, even to someone who has never heard of a tank shell before. Each one is different and they are all labelled to ensure you will not have problems in recognising and using the projectiles in game. Here are all the classes of shells!


[h1]Armour Piercing (AP)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/cb521d4eaec54c98c02b02795f081b1fab86746d.png[/img]

Standard armor piercing rounds without ballistic or armor piercing caps. AP shells are the most primitive way of making a projectile penetrate a hard surface. A chunk of metal is thrown at the armour to make a hole! The faster it goes, the more energy it strikes with, the more it penetrates - so it loses effectiveness over distance. At the beginning of WW2 most nations used an AP shell but as armor technology progressed, newer more advanced shell types were developed and issued.


[h1]Armor Piercing Capped (APC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/37edff51977108b210705ee892fd2b10a4912d3d.png[/img]

Standard armor piercing round with an armor piercing cap (AP + APC, abbreviated APC instead of APAPC). Armor piercing shells had a tendency to shatter when impacting armor that is thicker than the diameter of the shell. The addition of a cap (a soft material on the tip of the shell) helps reduce the shattering effect and allows the projectile to overcome armor in situations it would otherwise shatter and fail to penetrate.

The soft cap also helps to increase shells effectiveness against sloped armor. When a capped shells hit a armor plate at an angle, the cap deforms in the collision, allowing the projectile's center of mass to rotate into the armor's surface. This reduces the angle of attack and improves penetration.

Lastly, APC shells have increased penetration effectiveness against Face Hardened Armor (FHA) but reduced effectiveness against Rolled Homogeneous Armor (RHA). Homogeneous armor has the same thickness throughout, while face-hardened has a thin extremely hard layer. It's not a guarantee that different armor types (RHA & FHA) will be modeled in game, but it is something we may look into adding in the future.


[h1]Armor Piercing Capped Ballistic Capped (APCBC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/1ee0242b7feaecf713d846b9bafed743ec9760ed.png[/img]

These shells have all the same benefits and drawbacks of the standard APC shell with one exception, the addition of a ballistic cap. The ballistic cap (also known as a windscreen or windshield) helped reduce air resistance on the projectile. This helped increase the velocity and penetration of the shell at medium and long ranges.


[h1]Armor Piercing Ballistic Capped (APBC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/a41a1b719d56e30cc165712997271ff7151e00b3.png[/img]

The APBC shell is an untraditional flat nosed armor piercing projectile that is primarily used by the Soviets and was patterned after naval ammunition. What makes this type unique is the flat nose of the core which gives it better penetration against sloped armor than any other AP shell. The flat nose inside it helps dig into angled armor allowing the center of mass to rotate into the armor plate (just like the APC shell but with even better performance). Over time, the ballistic cap was added to counter poor aerodynamics of the flat nose, giving the shell better penetration at longer ranges.


[h1]Armor Piercing shells with High Explosive Filler (AP-HE, APC-HE, ABCBC-HE, APBC-HE)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/4e7a7d7154806eac8e31218ed918070d729f71cc.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/e6abfaf6ec04edcc270410e15c2e78c4b66546c7.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/56530e978e57657601d8cbe45d89c00fcb86e81e.png[/img]

Most of the previously mentioned shell types could come in two different forms: Solid shot or HE (High explosive filler). Solid shot is a just as it sounds, a standard projectile that is solid throughout. HE Filler adds increased damage to internal tank components after penetration. Shells with HE filler have slightly reduced penetration compared to their solid shot counterpart, but if they penetrate, they will cause more damage!


[h1]High Velocity shells (APCR, HVAP, APDS)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/d7725ab6f28f4784f6d745f98b266f9ba28f7def.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/61afd1ddacaf110f681481e087a478cf0754d519.png[/img]

Depending on the country of origin, they vary slightly in name and method of operation. These shells were designed to increase penetration potential through extreme velocity and hardness. All three shell types achieve increased penetration, but their weaknesses are poor performance against angled armor and they lose effectiveness dramatically over distance because they are light and rely on maximum kinetic energy for penetration.

Armor Piercing Composite Rigid shells (APCR) had a Tungsten core and was used by both the Germans and Soviets. Tungsten is a hard, high density material that is brittle but it is able to hit armor at high velocity and avoid shatter failure. High Velocity Armor Piercing shells (HVAP) is used by the Americans and is similar to APCR.

The British used Armor Piercing Discarding Sabot shells (APDS). It too had a hard core and when fired, the projectile sides fell off as the round as it exited the gun barrel releasing the sabot.  APDS maintains its velocity and penetration much longer than other Tungsten rounds due to its smaller in-flight diameter and reduced wind resistance, but it is the least accurate of the three.


[h1]High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/7294062c746a2b8f2c0c7c383285375533117cbc.png[/img]

“High Explosive Anti Tank” rounds are designed for guns that cannot shoot projectiles very fast, like short barreled cannons, artillery, and bazookas/rockets. A solution needed to be found to bypass the poor muzzle velocity. There is a shaped charge inside these rounds that concentrates the blast in a very small zone upon impact, launching towards the inside of the armoured target an explosion that generates a beam of molten metal or plasma. These shells are very deadly and do not lose penetration over distance, because the explosive is equally effective at any impact speed.

Side skirts and additional armour plates on tanks are a useful measure to stop these rounds, because the outer metal detonates the shell and the plasma beam does not reach the main armour protection. These shells are rare, so better to use them in the finest hour.


[h1]High Explosive (HE)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/b84ba5f79dd585b62d10c38f7cb57fd0b98fcbb1.png[/img]

HE rounds explode on impact and are great against soft targets like infantry and thin armour. They are also useful to destroy concrete and brick walls. Very big HE rounds are also capable of shredding tanks from the powerful blastwave.


[h1]How to choose your shell[/h1]
A tank will usually have a basic AP (with fillers or caps or a combination of everything :3 ) round, an “improved round” depending on the cannon type (HEAT for low velocity guns or ‘high velocity’ shells for high muzzle velocity guns), and finally a HE shell.

So if you’re shooting at infantry, emplacements, buildings or weak vehicles, always use HE. No brainer.

If you have a tank that you can beat, use your standard AP rounds. If your AP shell is capped (it will be correctly labelled) it will be great to use against sloped armour.

If you want to destroy a tank at long range or simply you do not have enough penetration because your gun is not made to shoot speedy projectiles, you can use HEAT. If you have APCR or other high velocity shells, these are great for penetrating armour that is too thick for your normal AP. These high velocity shells are also very comfortable to use because they are so fast you will not even have to apply lead to your target, but remember that all the ‘improved rounds’ are pathetic when it comes to sloped armour :P

See you next week with armour redesign!

[h1]Armor Piercing Capped (APC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/37edff51977108b210705ee892fd2b10a4912d3d.png[/img]

Standard armor piercing round with an armor piercing cap (AP + APC, abbreviated APC instead of APAPC). Armor piercing shells had a tendency to shatter when impacting armor that is thicker than the diameter of the shell. The addition of a cap (a soft material on the tip of the shell) helps reduce the shattering effect and allows the projectile to overcome armor in situations it would otherwise shatter and fail to penetrate.

The soft cap also helps to increase shells effectiveness against sloped armor. When a capped shells hit a armor plate at an angle, the cap deforms in the collision, allowing the projectile's center of mass to rotate into the armor's surface. This reduces the angle of attack and improves penetration.

Lastly, APC shells have increased penetration effectiveness against Face Hardened Armor (FHA) but reduced effectiveness against Rolled Homogeneous Armor (RHA). Homogeneous armor has the same thickness throughout, while face-hardened has a thin extremely hard layer. It's not a guarantee that different armor types (RHA & FHA) will be modeled in game, but it is something we may look into adding in the future.


[h1]Armor Piercing Capped Ballistic Capped (APCBC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/1ee0242b7feaecf713d846b9bafed743ec9760ed.png[/img]

These shells have all the same benefits and drawbacks of the standard APC shell with one exception, the addition of a ballistic cap. The ballistic cap (also known as a windscreen or windshield) helped reduce air resistance on the projectile. This helped increase the velocity and penetration of the shell at medium and long ranges.


[h1]Armor Piercing Ballistic Capped (APBC)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/a41a1b719d56e30cc165712997271ff7151e00b3.png[/img]

The APBC shell is an untraditional flat nosed armor piercing projectile that is primarily used by the Soviets and was patterned after naval ammunition. What makes this type unique is the flat nose of the core which gives it better penetration against sloped armor than any other AP shell. The flat nose inside it helps dig into angled armor allowing the center of mass to rotate into the armor plate (just like the APC shell but with even better performance). Over time, the ballistic cap was added to counter poor aerodynamics of the flat nose, giving the shell better penetration at longer ranges.


[h1]Armor Piercing shells with High Explosive Filler (AP-HE, APC-HE, ABCBC-HE, APBC-HE)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/4e7a7d7154806eac8e31218ed918070d729f71cc.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/e6abfaf6ec04edcc270410e15c2e78c4b66546c7.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/56530e978e57657601d8cbe45d89c00fcb86e81e.png[/img]

Most of the previously mentioned shell types could come in two different forms: Solid shot or HE (High explosive filler). Solid shot is a just as it sounds, a standard projectile that is solid throughout. HE Filler adds increased damage to internal tank components after penetration. Shells with HE filler have slightly reduced penetration compared to their solid shot counterpart, but if they penetrate, they will cause more damage!


[h1]High Velocity shells (APCR, HVAP, APDS)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/d7725ab6f28f4784f6d745f98b266f9ba28f7def.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/61afd1ddacaf110f681481e087a478cf0754d519.png[/img]

Depending on the country of origin, they vary slightly in name and method of operation. These shells were designed to increase penetration potential through extreme velocity and hardness. All three shell types achieve increased penetration, but their weaknesses are poor performance against angled armor and they lose effectiveness dramatically over distance because they are light and rely on maximum kinetic energy for penetration.

Armor Piercing Composite Rigid shells (APCR) had a Tungsten core and was used by both the Germans and Soviets. Tungsten is a hard, high density material that is brittle but it is able to hit armor at high velocity and avoid shatter failure. High Velocity Armor Piercing shells (HVAP) is used by the Americans and is similar to APCR.

The British used Armor Piercing Discarding Sabot shells (APDS). It too had a hard core and when fired, the projectile sides fell off as the round as it exited the gun barrel releasing the sabot.  APDS maintains its velocity and penetration much longer than other Tungsten rounds due to its smaller in-flight diameter and reduced wind resistance, but it is the least accurate of the three.


[h1]High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/7294062c746a2b8f2c0c7c383285375533117cbc.png[/img]

“High Explosive Anti Tank” rounds are designed for guns that cannot shoot projectiles very fast, like short barreled cannons, artillery, and bazookas/rockets. A solution needed to be found to bypass the poor muzzle velocity. There is a shaped charge inside these rounds that concentrates the blast in a very small zone upon impact, launching towards the inside of the armoured target an explosion that generates a beam of molten metal or plasma. These shells are very deadly and do not lose penetration over distance, because the explosive is equally effective at any impact speed.

Side skirts and additional armour plates on tanks are a useful measure to stop these rounds, because the outer metal detonates the shell and the plasma beam does not reach the main armour protection. These shells are rare, so better to use them in the finest hour.


[h1]High Explosive (HE)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/b84ba5f79dd585b62d10c38f7cb57fd0b98fcbb1.png[/img]

HE rounds explode on impact and are great against soft targets like infantry and thin armour. They are also useful to destroy concrete and brick walls. Very big HE rounds are also capable of shredding tanks from the powerful blastwave.


[h1]How to choose your shell[/h1]
A tank will usually have a basic AP (with fillers or caps or a combination of everything :3 ) round, an “improved round” depending on the cannon type (HEAT for low velocity guns or ‘high velocity’ shells for high muzzle velocity guns), and finally a HE shell.

So if you’re shooting at infantry, emplacements, buildings or weak vehicles, always use HE. No brainer.

If you have a tank that you can beat, use your standard AP rounds. If your AP shell is capped (it will be correctly labelled) it will be great to use against sloped armour.

If you want to destroy a tank at long range or simply you do not have enough penetration because your gun is not made to shoot speedy projectiles, you can use HEAT. If you have APCR or other high velocity shells, these are great for penetrating armour that is too thick for your normal AP. These high velocity shells are also very comfortable to use because they are so fast you will not even have to apply lead to your target, but remember that all the ‘improved rounds’ are pathetic when it comes to sloped armour :P

See you next week with armour redesign!

notes.title: Developer Blog #43 - Foxholes
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/19.png[/img]

Welcome to the 43th entry in our Devblog. It is time to talk about one of the new features of GoH - entrenchments.

Entrenchments are classified into two types: regular and engineering entrenchments. The latter type only come with field engineers or other unique units, and take more time to dig.


[h1]Foxholes[/h1]

Foxholes are a regular entrenchment that most infantrymen can build. It takes little time to build them and they give moderate protection from a prone position.  Most regular infantrymen can build a foxhole using their entrenching spade.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/15f7ca70fc615aeb4ab58a8767817038.png[/img]
HD [url=https://i.gyazo.com/15f7ca70fc615aeb4ab58a8767817038.png] link [/url]

[h1]Trench line[/h1]

Field engineers (not to be confused with miners) are not just responsible for setting up barbed wire fences, anti tank hedgehogs or other obstacles - they can now also dig infantry trenches! The trenches take much more time than a foxhole to dig but have numerous advantages - They can fit a whole squad, they offer more protection since soldiers can crouch behind it, and many of these trenches placed in a line will form a formidable line of defence! While some players won't like these defensive means because they prefer offensive moves, a well placed trench can be a key game changer especially in gamemodes like Frontlines.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/83cf8bb2f6e2bbaeb06c154cc48c5c79.png[/img]
HD [url=https://i.gyazo.com/83cf8bb2f6e2bbaeb06c154cc48c5c79.png] link [/url]

[h1]MG nest[/h1]

Your MG detachment comes with additional support infantry which in some cases are ammo carriers or close quarter assistants. The MG leader will either carry the MG in assault pose or carry it packed in it's tripod cradle for field-mounting it as an emplacement. While setting up, one of the mentioned assistants can dig a pit with suitable space for the tripod and the ammo carriers.


[h1]Mortar Pits[/h1]

Some field engineers can build a mortar pit which grants all-round protection for a medium mortar which also is set up automatically inside the pit. Moreover this deep pit has a shallow area for infantry positions. This entrenchment is unique and does not apply to regular mortars which just carry a small sandbag defence.


[h1]Tank Ditches[/h1]

Have you ever thought about how much you like a tank in a defensive viewpoint but you despise the terrible hull armour and can only use it in a hull-down position? Well, its time to build a tank ditch! They are built by field engineers and some are carried in special tanks as well ('veteran' tanks with special characteristics and experienced crews). A large portion of the hull is buried and so you have a much lower profile, in most cases with only the turret sticking out. Note that tanks can exit and enter the ditch and it doesnt turn them into sitting ducks.

More to come soon… Let us know if you have any particular entrenchment idea.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/e11f025ea8b7b390bf7d194365f071a6.png[/img]
HD [url=https://i.gyazo.com/e11f025ea8b7b390bf7d194365f071a6.png] link [/url]

notes.title: Developer Blog #42 - Tiger! [History Feature]
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/26.png[/img]

This friday we have something interesting (hopefully) to drive out for a spin. Since the recent tank history features were not too popular, we decided to showcase something a little more impressive this time. And what is more impressive than a Tiger

[h1]Panzerkampfwagen VI ‘Tiger’[/h1]

The Tiger was one of the most iconic and remarkable tanks of WW2. Initially deployed in North Africa and the region of Leningrad in 1942, the early versions showed many transmission problems and overall proved inadequate in swampy and also sandy terrains. In spite of all odds, the Russians were quickly impressed with the design and many designs were immediately rushed into design and production to counter the threat.

The Tiger was aimed to be superior in firepower, armour, technical advancements and weight to any other tank fielded at the time. It was made so, up to the point that it was expensive to manufacture, and hard to engineer. Some technical aspects of the tank were advanced for their time, which proved an advantage in combat but also a problem in the field because the crew were usually inexperienced in repairing, replacing or dismounting parts. This lead to many tanks being abandoned in combat, some even in a very good condition.

The Tiger traded engine power for firepower, and was both deadly in combat but severely underpowered with a 600/700hp engine to push 54 tonnes.

In 1943 the E version was fielded. With respect to it’s predecessor (the H), the E had all-metal rollers, a new gun cupola, extra armour on the mantlet and turret-ring and a long list of other changes.

In the Eastern Front in spring and summer seasons, and especially in the Western Front, the Tiger proved to be in it’s best hunting grounds. This is where it earned it’s name. 

[img]https://puu.sh/rexTQ/aca15610e5.jpg[/img]
HD [url=https://puu.sh/rexTQ/aca15610e5.jpg] link [/url]

[h1]In Gates of Hell[/h1]

In the game this beast is gorgeous in nearly all respects. A Tiger is always a milestone in a battle, it’s always there to leave a mark.  And we made a lot of effort in making her look and sound good, too :)

The gun is spectacular. Brilliant ballistics, good accuracy and dispersion. And the reload time is also very good for the gun’s size. 

The Tiger lacks a good power-to-weight ratio and as a result it accelerates slowly. Slopes are not Tiger’s friend. But it does not matter a lot, because it will surely pay off when it reaches the designated location. The Tiger is at it’s best when the enemies come to her. 

It’s a tank that has a very large skill cap. This means that experienced tankers in the tiger that can master it will surely make themselves be distinguishable. The Tiger’s armour is boxy, which means it’s perfect for angling. The ammunition’s choices are important, because they are multi-purpose. The tank is heavy and somewhat difficult to control in close quarters.

You will find the Tiger Ausf. H available from 1942 onwards and the Ausf. E from 1943 onwards. In addition, the ‘Hunting Tiger’ based on the E version, will be available from 1944 onwards.

[img]http://puu.sh/rke5W/c7377997fe.png[/img]
HD [url=http://puu.sh/rke5W/c7377997fe.png] link [/url]

[h1]’Hunting Tiger’[/h1]

Many tank aces like Michael Wittman earned their reputation aboard the Tiger. And it was well known that the best mechanics with the best commanders made the Tiger an extremely large threat to any tank in existence at the time. Hence we have decided to create a special version of the Tiger known as the ‘Hunting Tiger’. It is based on the E version, and has some improvements over a regular Tiger. First, it is covered in camouflage, which grants it a concealment advantage. Next, the Hunting Tiger has a faster rotating turret and a better accuracy for it’s gun. A skilled marksman can zero the aiming device on his tank with greater speed and precision, making it an extremely useful tank amongst heavies, almost converting it to a tank destroyer in that respect.

[img]https://puu.sh/rkfCs/7ba06c8e51.png[/img]
HD [url=https://puu.sh/rkfCs/7ba06c8e51.png] link [/url]

[img]https://puu.sh/rkfEx/51f70dd793.png[/img]
HD [url=https://puu.sh/rkfEx/51f70dd793.png] link [/url]


[h1]Panzer VI Ausf. E Statistics:[/h1]

[b]Main armament[/b]: 88mm Kwk.36, L/56
[b]Penetration at 100m[/b]: 
[list]
[*]151-138mm (APCBC-HE)
[*]200-179mm (APCR)
[*]110mm (HEAT)
[/list]
[b]Armour[/b]:
[list]
[*]110-80mm (Turret)
[*]100-82mm (Hull)
[/list]
[b]Power[/b]: 700hp
[b]Weight and power/weight[/b]: 54 tonnes, 12.8hp/ton
[b]Top speed[/b]:
[list]
[*]40km/h (On-road)
[*]19km/h (Off-road)
[/list]
[b]Gun handling[/b]:
[list]
[*]0,65 Accuracy rating
[*]3s zeroing time
[*]0,21 dispersion value
[/list]

This friday we have something interesting (hopefully) to drive out for a spin. Since the recent tank history features were not too popular, we decided to showcase something a little more impressive this time. And what is more impressive than a Tiger

[h1]Panzerkampfwagen VI ‘Tiger’[/h1]

The Tiger was one of the most iconic and remarkable tanks of WW2. Initially deployed in North Africa and the region of Leningrad in 1942, the early versions showed many transmission problems and overall proved inadequate in swampy and also sandy terrains. In spite of all odds, the Russians were quickly impressed with the design and many designs were immediately rushed into design and production to counter the threat.

The Tiger was aimed to be superior in firepower, armour, technical advancements and weight to any other tank fielded at the time. It was made so, up to the point that it was expensive to manufacture, and hard to engineer. Some technical aspects of the tank were advanced for their time, which proved an advantage in combat but also a problem in the field because the crew were usually inexperienced in repairing, replacing or dismounting parts. This lead to many tanks being abandoned in combat, some even in a very good condition.

The Tiger traded engine power for firepower, and was both deadly in combat but severely underpowered with a 600/700hp engine to push 54 tonnes.

In 1943 the E version was fielded. With respect to it’s predecessor (the H), the E had all-metal rollers, a new gun cupola, extra armour on the mantlet and turret-ring and a long list of other changes.

In the Eastern Front in spring and summer seasons, and especially in the Western Front, the Tiger proved to be in it’s best hunting grounds. This is where it earned it’s name. 

[img]https://puu.sh/rexTQ/aca15610e5.jpg[/img]
HD [url=https://puu.sh/rexTQ/aca15610e5.jpg] link [/url]

[h1]In Gates of Hell[/h1]

In the game this beast is gorgeous in nearly all respects. A Tiger is always a milestone in a battle, it’s always there to leave a mark.  And we made a lot of effort in making her look and sound good, too :)

The gun is spectacular. Brilliant ballistics, good accuracy and dispersion. And the reload time is also very good for the gun’s size. 

The Tiger lacks a good power-to-weight ratio and as a result it accelerates slowly. Slopes are not Tiger’s friend. But it does not matter a lot, because it will surely pay off when it reaches the designated location. The Tiger is at it’s best when the enemies come to her. 

It’s a tank that has a very large skill cap. This means that experienced tankers in the tiger that can master it will surely make themselves be distinguishable. The Tiger’s armour is boxy, which means it’s perfect for angling. The ammunition’s choices are important, because they are multi-purpose. The tank is heavy and somewhat difficult to control in close quarters.

You will find the Tiger Ausf. H available from 1942 onwards and the Ausf. E from 1943 onwards. In addition, the ‘Hunting Tiger’ based on the E version, will be available from 1944 onwards.

[img]http://puu.sh/rke5W/c7377997fe.png[/img]
HD [url=http://puu.sh/rke5W/c7377997fe.png] link [/url]

[h1]’Hunting Tiger’[/h1]

Many tank aces like Michael Wittman earned their reputation aboard the Tiger. And it was well known that the best mechanics with the best commanders made the Tiger an extremely large threat to any tank in existence at the time. Hence we have decided to create a special version of the Tiger known as the ‘Hunting Tiger’. It is based on the E version, and has some improvements over a regular Tiger. First, it is covered in camouflage, which grants it a concealment advantage. Next, the Hunting Tiger has a faster rotating turret and a better accuracy for it’s gun. A skilled marksman can zero the aiming device on his tank with greater speed and precision, making it an extremely useful tank amongst heavies, almost converting it to a tank destroyer in that respect.

notes.title: Developer Blog #41 - Multiplayer number Two
notes.content:
[img]http://puu.sh/qXw1A/be4a882467.png[/img]

Welcome back to the friday weekly Devblog, It’s time to continue our collection of multiplayer entries. I know what all of you are thinking - oh my! It’s actually been one week after the previous devblog, they might actually be on schedule again :)


[h1]Frontline[/h1]

Frontline is one of the classic game-modes of all time and it would be a crime against tradition to remove it.

In Frontline, the first team is ordered to attack the enemy lines, and naturally the second team defends. Roles reverse for a second fight afterwards. An array of flags are captured as the forces advance into enemy territory.

We have not executed changes to this game-mode yet. It is very straightforward and there is little room to add additional features, because the pace of these battles is very frenetic. Making it more hectic is the least of our intentions.

Therefore we would like to hear what you have to say. Tell us your ideas about how to improve this game-mode in the comments section down below. The most feasible ideas that make the gameplay more enjoyable will be considered for implementing.


[h1]Territory[/h1]

This new game-mode is aimed to become one of the core game-modes of Gates of Hell and it is an attempt to reach the maximum representation of a WW2 situation while keeping it competitive for tournaments and e-sports. 

The maps are split into multiple sectors that cover the entire surface area. These sectors require infantry to be captured, and each grant the players with points to win the game, like in Assault Zones. Key strategic areas like cities have more, smaller sectors (all zones are as valuable though) which means that the player who can dominate key map areas will have a massive point income advantage because there are more zones under his control, despite maybe controlling a smaller % of the map. 

Unlike Assault Zones, which only has limited capturable areas along the map, in Territory the whole map is disputed. This means that the entire frontline is moving, and that attacks can be more unpredictable from any direction in the conquest of more sectors of the map.

Many players will rejoice in that they plan to send an entire soviet penal battalion to charge the entire map. Aha - last but not least, in Territory you also gain points for killing enemy troops! So massive suicide charges will bring a lot of joy to enemy MG emplacements as well. The games will be won by being able to outplay your opponents and dominate the map inch by inch, as well as lowering your casualties and inflicting terrible damage to your opponent. This is war, keep your men alive, and capture the positions!

Territory is a game-mode we plan to introduce from the initial betas as well.

[img]http://puu.sh/qXw46/e91bed91d1.png[/img]
HD [url=http://puu.sh/qXw46/e91bed91d1.png] link [/url]

notes.title: Developer Blog #40 - Multiplayer number One.
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/29.png[/img]

Welcome back to the Devblog, today we will say a few things about multiplayer. These devblog entries will continue for a couple of weeks. Each time, we will talk about improving one existing multiplayer game-mode and announcing a new one :)

[h1]Classic game-modes[/h1]

In Gates of Hell we will conserve the original game-modes that people have been enjoying throughout the Men of War games, with some changes.

[h1]Control Zones[/h1]

‘Control Points’, ‘Battlezones’ or ‘Assault Zones’, this game-mode is the most popular and probably the only one with it’s name having changed a couple of times.

In Gates of Hell, we wish to promote this game-mode as one of the most played, but also make small adaptations to ensure that it is more loyal to a WW2 environment.

This game-mode is played by capturing strategic zones that are placed along the map. The side with a larger number of capped zones earns points. Instead of placing the zones as arbitrary circles distributed along the map, the shapes can also be now poligonal in many maps to define real strategic locations, such as building blocks, railway stations, etc.  They can be large or small.

[img]http://puu.sh/qPg0E/bce1526fd9.jpg[/img]
HD [url=http://puu.sh/qPg0E/bce1526fd9.jpg] link [/url]

In addition, for some maps, there will be one or two ‘crossing the fence’ zones. These zones are particularly demanding to capture by any of the teams and the player must show a flawless display of dominance to capture. What makes these zones unique is that the capping area is different for both teams. The players must advance deeper into enemy territory to claim the capture point instead of a regular central position by the flag where the zone is disputed by both teams. Since the enemy will have already arrived to the location where you are supposed to capture, it is much harder to breach through. 

Finally, this game-mode will be enhanced with additional in-game features that will also vary from map to map, such as periodic artillery bombardments along specific areas, secondary objectives, etc. These will also be as balanced as possible to make it as damaging or beneficial, equally for all teams.

[img]http://puu.sh/qPg28/b9b4a9121e.jpg[/img]
HD [url=http://puu.sh/qPg28/b9b4a9121e.jpg] link [/url]

All in all we aim to increase the dynamism of the game-mode from map to map. These changes will also bring more authenticity to the WW2 stamp on the game-mode, by defining real strategic locations to capture. 

Assault Zones is a game-mode that you will have access to immediately


[h1]Escort Run[/h1]

This new game-mode is a two-round scenario where one of the team’s goal is to take a convoy of fuel trucks to their destination, while the opposing side must ambush them. It is one of the game-modes where ambush tactics must be used at it’s fullest extent. The escorting team will have access to motorised units and vehicles, while the ambushing side will deploy infantry, guns, and artillery. In the arranged period of time, each fuel truck that manages to pass through will score a point. The roles will reverse upon finishing the first round.

Escort Run is one of the game-modes that we plan to introduce already in the first betas of Gates of Hell.

notes.title: Developer Blog #38 - T-26 [History Feature]
notes.content:
[img]https://puu.sh/qhyP7/8b4e973ce7.png[/img]

Today is Friday and this week’s devblog is once again part of the History Feature Series. Today we will talk about the T-26: The tank’s history and review its performance in the game.


[h1]Development[/h1]

In the end of the 1920s the USSR began the development of the new generation of tanks that would compose the core of the russian armed tank divisions almost exclusively until 1941. 

Development of the highly exported british Vickers 6-ton resulted in the T-26 standard light tank. Several versions were built, such as the 2-turreted T-26s, the flamethrower OT-26, and multiple versions of the main T-26 armed with a 45mm gun.

About 10,000 T-26s were built. The mass increased to nearly 10 tonnes but despite any drawbacks the T-26 was a general improvement from the original Vickers 6-ton, especially with regard to the armament.

The type 20K 45mm gun was very successful at the time of it's first introduction and showed good performance at the Spanish Civil War, when the USSR sent multiple tanks to aid the Republican side of the conflict. Clearly superior to the Panzer Is and italian tankettes that it faced in Spain, many T-26s ended in the hands of the Fascist nationalists which re-used them again.

By the Winter War in 1939 and operation Barbarossa the T-26 was outdated, but still saw a long combat service until 1945 in the USSR and longer in other nations that used captured or bought variants. When WW2 began the tank was beginning to appear underpowered and definitely too fragile with its thin armour. After 1941 it also demonstrated to be undergunned for the german tanks that were being manufactured from that point on.


[h1]In Gates of Hell[/h1]

In Gates of Hell the russian early light tanks are divided into two branches: The rapid firing autocannon branch of tanks armed with 12,7 and 20mm automatic weapons, and the series of light tanks which use the standard 45mm 20K cannon. The T-26 belongs to the latter category. It can be fielded until the year 1943 when it is replaced by the T-70.

The T-26 isn’t particularly fast like the BT series which also have paper armour and the same 45mm gun. Some players will also prefer the autocannon branch of light tanks to this one. So all in all the T26 forms an ugly portrait to the eyes of the players. 

To compensate, the T-26 can be bought extremely early and it is very affordable. This makes it forgiving to play in this tank, in addition it is a good option against similar german tanks (Panzer 38t, Panzer II). In conclusion, this tank is very adequate for inexperienced players or risky manoeuvres.

In addition, of course we made the T-26 look pretty, detailed and gorgeous. Who knows, maybe that makes it more appealing in the game!


[h1]T-26 Mod.39 Statistics:[/h1]

[b]Main armament[/b]: 45mm 20-K
[b]Penetration at 100m[/b]: 
[list]
[*]50-45mm (APBC)
[*]60-55mm (APCR)
[/list]
[b]Armour[/b]:
[list]
[*]15-10mm (Turret)
[*]15mm (Hull)
[/list]
[b]Power[/b]: 4 cylinder Armstrong siddeley, 90hp
[b]Weight and power/weight[/b]: 9.6 tonnes, 9.4hp/ton
[b]Top speed[/b]:
[list]
[*]31km/h (On-road)
[*]22km/h (Off-road)
[/list]

HD [url=http://puu.sh/qhyVu/28da609492.png.png] link [/url]

notes.title: Developer Blog #36 - Fire and smoke
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/27.png[/img]

Hello and welcome back to the “weekly” entry of the developer blog.

[h1]Muzzles[/h1]

We have redesigned all muzzle effects for guns, tanks, artillery, rocket launchers, etc.

The idea is to create a vast array of different muzzles to be used on different tanks. Many tanks, especially those with powerful guns or strong recoil, have a variety of muzzle brakes, designed to use the energy of the blastwave for example to lower the recoil, increase stability, increase range, protect the fighting compartment from gases, or other functions. Muzzle brakes can also vary in shape and form.

It is therefore evident that the smoke is projected in many different ways depending on the gun, and this is why we have different special effects.

[img]http://puu.sh/pLqCn/4f3670db72.png[/img]

[h1]Dust[/h1]

Tanks passing by, explosions, firing large guns and other combat events cause the ground to shake and lift dust from the dirt. The dust clouds also take time to settle.

We have tried to implement this as realistically as possible to portray the effects of devastation and overall battle ambient. In heavy battles it will be hard to observe with full clarity the overall ground layer and cover if explosions are continuously going on nearby - this can be also used as a tactical strategy.

[h1]Echoes[/h1]

As well as tremendous and fierce sounds nearby, explosions and large guns produce echoes that can be heard at long distances. Since it is possible you won’t be able to see the artillery that is firing over your troops, you can judge how far it is located from the pitch and intensity of the echo. The intensified stereo effect will also be able to guide you to the direction of the source of the sound.

[img]http://puu.sh/pMS3l/af9229cc7f.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Blog #35 - E3 edition / Barbarossa anniversary
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10379584/e467910f1474fa694adb133999fe28477c768f95.png[/img]

It is an important date this week, since yesterday marked the 75th anniversary of the beginning of the Eastern Front / Great Patriotic War. In addition, last week was the E3 event. So we have some news to hand out today that might be worth the interest of many.

[h1]Human behaviour[/h1]

The core AI has been updated in some areas, which is good news for everybody but it’s not time to talk about that. The human behaviour, on the other hand, is the focus of today’s news. Weapon handling has become more realistic. The player, when shifting the orientation of the gun, walking or running, receiving a hit, or other activities that demand turning one’s attention or cause disturbance when aiming; mean that you need to zero the target to narrow the accuracy again. This means, that the AI tends to aim instead of firing immediately, when there is an enemy ensight. 

Naturally, bipod or tripod mounted MGs, on the other hand, are more accurate immediately after shifting position and thus are better suppression weapons.

The ‘aimbot’ factor now represents true human behaviour and this is a first step to many in the future.

Work has gone into melee attacks. It is now possible to visualise real charges of infantry and the AI will use their bayonets, knives, fists and guns to fight in short ranges. More information on this will be dispatched in the future.

[h1]Crucial battles[/h1]


Crucial battles is a new online PvP gamemode. It is the first announcement of a new multiplayer development! The concept of this gamemode is to combine competitive gameplay with historical locations and battles. This playstyle will be only for the ones that appreciate history and get ready to face any odds!

In Crucial Battles there is no room for defying historical layouts. The unit roster for each battle will be accurate in size with respect to the real events. This means that in many occasions one of the armies will be heavily outnumbering the other, like it occurred during the war! In such case, to enable balanced gameplay, the objectives to win will be made so that the unit unbalance is compensated upon by easier objectives or other strategic superiorities.

Each Crucial Battle map is different because battles were fought on various conditions and situations, so the objectives of each separate scenario will be different, depending on the battle it reenacts. 

In addition, each Crucial Battle multiplayer scenario will have an array of special units for the different factions that will be developed for that precise multiplayer battle. This includes naval boats, super heavy mortars, coastal battery guns, or other machinery that was used in the historical fight. It would be obviously unbalanced to include these in the usual multiplayer unit list for regular game modes, but Crucial Battles is an excellent opportunity to visualize how these monsters can behave in their entourage.

It is important to point out that it takes a lot of time to develop and balance Crucial Battles scenarios and their assets, thus we will release them gradually with time. However all Crucial Battle releases, whereas from the start or developed after release, will be included in the base game [b]for free[/b].

notes.title: Developer Blog #34 - Happy D-day!
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/34.png[/img]

Welcome back to the "weekly" routine of Devblogs.

Yes, you may have noticed for the last 3 weeks or so there was no devblog. The reason for such lack of updates are related to our publisher. In the coming weeks everything will become apparent. Having said this however, the development of GoH has been uninterrupted and we have quite important announcements to make:


[h1]D day[/h1]

It is the 72nd anniversary of D day. In the 6th of June 1944, the largest landing operation in history of warfare, codenamed Overlord, began.

Although it will be a very long journey until the western front is modelled in GoH, you can see a sneak peek of what is to come below. All bunkers have interactible inner passages and rooms, which can be easily managed because the roofs are made see-through as the player enters the superstructures.

[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/render1.1.png[/img]

[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/render2.1.png[/img]

[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/render3.png[/img]



[h1]Material technology[/h1]

We have begun quite a large re-structuration of game resources (environment 3d models), which has been made possible due to the new material systems developed for Gem2.3. The whole process is being carried out quite confidentially, and the plans were laid on paper since Christmas. It is estimated the texture memory will be optimised by a 50% when the whole process is over. Not only this, but the actual quality and appearance of the visuals has also been given a push forward with this process.

The new changes, when complete, will be of great aid for lower-end PCs and also contribute to the performance that affects all machines.


Next week we will talk a bit about human behaviour and AI.

notes.title: Developer Blog #33 - Panzer IB [History Feature]
notes.content:
Developer Blog #33 - Panzer IB [History Feature]

[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/33.png[/img]

[h1]Welcome back to the weekly blog of Gates of Hell.[/h1]

Today is Friday and this week’s devblog is fully dedicated again to the History Feature Series. Today we will go over the Panzerkampfwagen I Ausf. B, talk about the unit’s history and review its performance in the game.

[h1]Development[/h1]

The Panzerkampfwagen I, or Pz.Kpfw I (Armoured Fighting Vehicle Mark I) was the first armoured vehicle produced by the German Army after WWI. It’s real designation (officially) is Sd.kfz. 101, which is the abbreviation of Sonderkraftfahrzeug meaning special ordnance vehicle.

The design paperwork started in 1932 (before Hitler came to power) but it’s mass production saw the light two years later. Guderian’s plan to make suitable fighting vehicles, approved by Hitler, included a test prototype for training tank crews and exploring tactics, which became the Panzer I. Eventually the designs of Guderian’s plan culminated with the design of Panzer IIIs and IVs which had many factors taken into consideration from lessons from the Panzer Is and IIs.

It’s design philosophy is very early in terms of WW2 specifications and would not represent the tank construction requirements that would be evident after the start of WW2, such as actually carrying a main gun and armour capable of blocking anything above a rifle caliber projectile. The Panzer I saw action during the Spanish Civil War in the hands of the Fascist insurgent army, and also in early WW2 campaigns. Some Panzer I As were sold to China. However, it’s potential in battle was very limited by firepower and armour, since the idea was that the Panzer I tanks were utilised for training purposes exclusively in the hands of Panzerwaffe cadettes.

In the time of it’s construction, the Panzer I was not capable of matching the other nations’ equivalents like the T26 of the USSR, instead the Panzer I had a different role of supporting infantry and training crews, and was never meant to confront its rivals face to face, and in Gates of Hell you will not want to face off another armoured vehicle with this tank.

The Panzer I chassis was used for the development of other tank destroyers and self-propelled guns (each will have their own devblog), and after many were re-equipped, the old turrets were re-commissioned at the Atlantic Wall bunkers.

[h1]In Gates of Hell[/h1]

In Gates of Hell the Panzer I Ausf.B will be an infantry support and scouting vehicle, maneuverable and nimble, but with low power-to-weight ratio, thus it is hard to climb slopes with it. It will be the first vehicle the player can have access to when playing in Multiplayer as Germany for the years 1939-41. The cost for purchasing this vehicle in multiplayer is low, and it is an excellent weapon to harass enemy infantry with, denying the entire area to the enemy thanks to suppressing fire from the double MG34.

The mobility is acceptable and overall the statistics make it a suitable infantry support vehicle for the early game in early war settings.

[h1]Hey folks, welcome back to the Friday’s Odyssey :).[/h1]

This week there has been internal testing going on within the devs. The game is playable though still it needs a lot of development. This means the gameplay trailer, in some shape or form, can be now made for the upcoming week.

You may or may not have noticed, we updated the ‘To Berlin’ trailer as well.

[h1]3D Modellers.[/h1]

We are looking for 3D modellers to speed up the production process. If you are interested, please get in touch, via messaging the devs on Steam, or email to barbedwire.dev@gmail.com

Once you get in contact we can sort out which kinds of models you want to do and talk about the details. 

[h1]Multiplayer Coalitions.[/h1]

Many people requested to allow players to choose factions within their parties in multiplayer lobbies. This is in progress and will start to become used when we add the 3rd faction after Early Access. Hence people without DLCs can always play any match since they will have the necessary minimum factions to play Axis vs Allies anyways, with the condition that the year-setting allows that faction to exist in the period, and as long as the host allows you. No comrades are left behind!

notes.title: Developer Blog #27 - Achtung Panzer! Part I
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/27.png[/img]

[h1]Welcome back. Why don’t we talk about tanks in greater detail?.[/h1]

We aim to give a new feeling to the entire tank combat and handling. Realistically remaking how tanks play, feel, and move.

[h1]True Acceleration[/h1]

One does not simply accelerate a 60 ton beast to it’s maximum speed in a mere 2 seconds. We are completely ripping apart this abomination of tank motion and implementing realistic acceleration. The main factor for this feature is horsepower/ton. For example, light tanks with powerful engines have good acceleration. Others, mainly heavy beasts with mediocre engines, will suffer from slow acceleration.

[h1]Braking distance.[/h1]

If you try to slow down a 50 ton tank moving 40km/h in 1 second, the deceleration damping that the crew will suffer should cause deep injuries and probably death, and damage to the internal vehicle’s modules. Moreover, if the tracks stop suddenly, the tank would still move forward bursting through the ground because of the momentum it carries. We are in the process of implementing realistic stopping distance, which will be vary mainly depending on the mass of the vehicles. Poking through corners in heavy tanks is now harder! 

[h1]On-road and off-road[/h1]

In reality, tanks are much more mobile on road than off-road. The soft terrain caused tracks to bury into the soil and required more energy to move. In the past vehicles in Gem2-engine based games had similar top speeds regardless of the terrain they went through. Not any more. If you want to go fast, find a suitable road to drive through. We plan to implement more specific calculations to off-road and on-road speeds. The T-34, for example, had a very good off-road movement compared to on-road. The light Panzer II, on the other hand, had a pathetic off-road motion.

[h1]Turret rotation[/h1]

We have set real speeds for turret movement. Electrically and hydraulically powered turrets have very respectable turret motion. Manually rotated turrets are, however, not that satisfying. So for the oldschool arm-powered turrets, ensure they are facing the right direction from the start!

notes.title: Developer Blog #27 - Achtung Panzer! Part I
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/27.png[/img]

[h1]Welcome back. Why don’t we talk about tanks in greater detail?.[/h1]

We aim to give a new feeling to the entire tank combat and handling. Realistically remaking how tanks play, feel, and move.

[h1]True Acceleration[/h1]

One does not simply accelerate a 60 ton beast to it’s maximum speed in a mere 2 seconds. We are completely ripping apart this abomination of tank motion and implementing realistic acceleration. The main factor for this feature is horsepower/ton. For example, light tanks with powerful engines have good acceleration. Others, mainly heavy beasts with mediocre engines, will suffer from slow acceleration.

[h1]Braking distance.[/h1]

If you try to slow down a 50 ton tank moving 40km/h in 1 second, the deceleration damping that the crew will suffer should cause deep injuries and probably death, and damage to the internal vehicle’s modules. Moreover, if the tracks stop suddenly, the tank would still move forward bursting through the ground because of the momentum it carries. We are in the process of implementing realistic stopping distance, which will be vary mainly depending on the mass of the vehicles. Poking through corners in heavy tanks is now harder! 

[h1]On-road and off-road[/h1]

In reality, tanks are much more mobile on road than off-road. The soft terrain caused tracks to bury into the soil and required more energy to move. In the past vehicles in Gem2-engine based games had similar top speeds regardless of the terrain they went through. Not any more. If you want to go fast, find a suitable road to drive through. notes.title: Developer Blog #25
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/17.png[/img]

[h1]Oh it’s you again. Welcome back to the Blog. It’s gonna be a short one this week, but at least it’s punchy! [/h1]

[h1]Sky technology[/h1]

We have put a lot of effort in conveying a new atmosphere and mood. The sky box has been revamped with new HD ambient, which is backed by the HDR post-process on top. Harmonious colours and realistic environments aid to construct an image that conveys more stylized and also more impacting scenery.

[h1]Blending fog[/h1]

In addition, the edges of the map now blend with new fog shaders aimed to eliminate the awkward hard edging that occurred on different camera angles between the land and the sky. Once again a step forward towards making the bigger picture of immersion and visual attractiveness that we want to craft in Gates of Hell.

[h1]Media update[/h1]

The first 5 new screenshots are out! You can check them out in the store page.
You may also be able to appreciate some of the new skies in there with the advancements that are described above.

Next step is the [b]two[/b]
 trailers. Yes. Two.

notes.title: Developer Blog #24 - Getting there...
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/24.1.png[/img]

[h1]Hello friends and players. Exciting news for this devblog entry.[/h1]

[h1]Mac and Linux[/h1]

Mac and Linux are now supported! This means no longer will the game be restricted for Windows only. Many requests were made over the years to support other OS and at last has this been achieved.

[h1]Cross Platform[/h1]

One of the features of Gates of Hell game engine is that it has become cross platform and people will be able to play against each other independently of what OS they are running. The servers for Multiplayer are all centralised, hence there will be no advantage for any particular platform over another if the specs are similar.

[b]Wait… that’s all?[/b]
[i]‘You kept us in the dark for 2 weeks and all you say is this?’[/i]

… Hehe...

[h1]Store Update[/h1]

We’re going to update the store page! This means we will bring in new screenshots, new videos, etc. In the first place, we will revamp the trailer. Next, release a gameplay/introduction video to Gates of Hell. In addition, several new screenshots will hit the showcase slider.

We are still working on all this, and we can’t give you an exact day in which it will be all up. It will be gradually uploaded along the next 1-2 weeks.

notes.title: Developer Blog #18 - Merry Christmas!
notes.content:
[img]http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/12.png[/img]

[h1]Welcome back to the 18th Devblog[/h1]

This Devblog entry will be in fact, the last one of 2015. Next week the team will be on vacations, equally we will leave the readers to kindly celebrate the upcoming new year with friends and family.

[h1]Tank Mobility.[/h1]

Time and effort has been invested in producing a realistic tank mobility system. We have simulated true acceleration and braking systems for tanks, of which their mass, horsepower, traverse speed, etc is all considered. You will feel when a tank is heavy. Our next step is to model the mobility capabilities over different terrain, to give a huge advantage to going through solid ground and the drawbacks of going cross-country. I’m sure you will think twice about buying a heavy tank on a rainy autumn muddy map. It will have an important impact on gameplay, especially within the competitive community. It will be one more factor to take into account to buying units, which also is map-specific depending on the terrain. And for those that question the importance or historical accuracy of this feature in a WW2 game, I’ll just point you in the direction of this Wehrmacht soldier who has many beautiful things to say about Russia when it gets muddy.
[img]http://www.ww2incolor.com/d/442241-4/1_044[/img]


[h1]It’s a trap![/h1]

We have designed the playstyle of urban areas to be played as much outside as inside the buildings or ruins. This will differentiate the urban maps from any others in the fact that cover, intricate wall parts, etc can be used to hide and ambush the enemy, ensuring the player can prove himself in close quarters like never seen before. You will value every inch of land you secure within the debris, plus you must become proficient in assessing when (and where) the enemy will try to flank you, to play ahead of the game. It’s either you or your enemy who will fall into the trap!

[img]http://media.moddb.com/cache/images/groups/1/19/18139/thumb_620x2000/18.jpg[/img]
HD [url=http://media.moddb.com/images/groups/1/19/18139/18.jpg] link [/url]


And that’s as far as we will take it this year Folks. We wish you a merry Christmas and a happy new year, and we will see you back on 2016!
